mcq: Complete the statement from the course material: "______ refers to matters in existence when the new legislation comes into force does not necessarily make that provision retrospective."
Merely because a statutory provision refers to matters in existence when the new legislation comes into force does not necessarily make that provision retrospective.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are the Companies and Allied Matters Act and Income Tax Acts."
Examples are the Companies and Allied Matters Act and Income Tax Acts.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is the date the Act becomes operative."
The date of commencement is the date the Act becomes operative.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ are any Order, Rules, Bye-Laws made before or after the commencement of an Act in exercise of powers conferred by an Act."
Subsidiary instruments are any Order, Rules, Bye-Laws made before or after the commencement of an Act in exercise of powers conferred by an Act.
Complete the statement from the course material: "______ is an essential feature of any Bill being drafted for introduction into the Legislature."
A long title is an essential feature of any Bill being drafted for introduction into the Legislature.
fib: ______ is a clause in the preliminary provisions.
The best place is a clause in the preliminary provisions.
______ is a statutory provision designed to help users find their way around legislation.
A road map clause is a statutory provision designed to help users find their way around legislation.
______ is used in the defined term; the definition uses a noun.
A verb is used in the defined term; the definition uses a noun.
______ is the name by which the law is to be identified and cited.
The short title is the name by which the law is to be identified and cited.
______ are used today rather less than in the past; many drafters consider them to be redundant.
Preambles are used today rather less than in the past; many drafters consider them to be redundant.
